source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Identify all areas or aspects of the building fire-safety check that failed.
3. Document date and time of inspection.
4. List each failed item or section according to its location within the building.
5. Clearly describe the deficiency or non-compliance observed.
6. Include photographs or diagrams where applicable to better illustrate the issue.
7. Note the relevant fire safety codes (NFPA, IFC, etc.) or local regulations that were violated. Include the specific code sections.
8. Record notes from discussions with the building owner or manager.
9. Note recommended corrective actions or remediation needed for compliance.
10. Include the name and title of the inspector, along with signature or electronic approval.
11. Attach or include references to previous inspections or reports if the issue is a repeat offense.
12. Indicate any immediate hazards and describe any actions taken to mitigate these (e.g., evacuation, shutting down systems).
13. Provide a clear timeline for compliance
